candidates.name: RSS
candidates.headline: The feed survived the reader. The open web kept sending updates.
candidates.why_survives: Feed readers can still collect new articles directly from sites without a social-media timeline.
candidates.where_now: Thunderbird continues to document built-in support for RSS and Atom subscriptions.
candidates.note: RSS is a family of feed formats, not a single discontinued product. The support article establishes ongoing functionality, not usage share.

rating.note: Editorial score; images and device review required before promotion.

candidates.name: INTERNET RELAY CHAT
candidates.headline: Before the chat apps, there were channels. People are still in them.
candidates.why_survives: Volunteer-run networks and open-source project communities continue to use the IRC protocol.
candidates.where_now: Libera Chat operates an IRC network for free software and collaborative projects.
candidates.note: IRC is a protocol, not one surviving application. Libera Chat is a current example, not a claim that every historic IRC network survives or that usage is growing. Supporting sources: https://libera.chat/ and https://libera.chat/about/

rating.note: Editorial score; images and device review required before promotion.

candidates.name: ATLANTIC HORSESHOE CRABS
candidates.headline: An ancient body plan still leaves tracks on Atlantic beaches.
candidates.why_survives: Coastal habitat, spawning beaches and managed harvest help sustain surviving populations.
candidates.where_now: Atlantic horseshoe crabs still spawn on US shores, including Delaware Bay.
candidates.note: Ancient lineage does not mean the modern species is unchanged for hundreds of millions of years. They are not true crabs. Conservation status varies by region; avoid implying that survival means secure populations. Habitat and harvest context: https://www.fisheries.noaa.gov/feature-story/horseshoe-crabs-managing-resource-birds-bait-and-blood

rating.note: Editorial score; images and device review required before promotion.

candidates.name: FAX
candidates.headline: Email took over. The fax number kept receiving documents.
candidates.why_survives: Online fax services connect digital workflows to fax numbers, keeping the communication format usable.
candidates.where_now: eFax offers sending and receiving through email, browsers and mobile devices.
candidates.note: Scope includes online fax, not only standalone machines. A current service establishes functionality, not market size. Survival explanation is an editorial inference from interoperability. No security or legal necessity claim. Supporting hardware listing: https://www.brother-usa.com/p/fax-machines/FAX2840 (out of stock when checked).

rating.note: Editorial score; images and device review required before promotion.

candidates.name: QUEEN MARY 2 CROSSINGS
candidates.headline: The jet won the race. An ocean liner still offers the crossing.
candidates.why_survives: Cunard sells the crossing as a journey and holiday experience rather than the fastest route across the Atlantic.
candidates.where_now: Queen Mary 2 continues Cunard transatlantic crossings between Southampton and New York.
candidates.note: Checked 8 October 2026: the operator advertises Queen Mary 2 transatlantic voyages, including 2026–2028. This is a surviving service, not the original Queen Mary or QE2 in active service. The explanation is editorial inference from Cunard’s experience-led offering; no passenger or profitability trend is asserted.

rating.note: Editorial rating after checking the linked primary source. Image and device review remain pending.

candidates.name: FOUNTAIN PENS
candidates.headline: The keyboard took the desk. The nib kept its place.
candidates.why_survives: Refillable ink systems, replaceable nibs and repair services keep fountain pens useful for handwriting.
candidates.where_now: Pelikan still offers fountain pens, bottled inks and repair services in its current collection.
candidates.note: A current manufacturer catalogue establishes an ongoing product and support offering, not sales growth or worldwide usage. The survival explanation is an editorial inference from refillability and repair support.

rating.note: Editorial score; images and device review required before promotion.

candidates.name: GOPHER
candidates.headline: Before the web had pages, it had menus. Some of those menus are still here.
candidates.why_survives: Community hosts and compatible text clients preserve access to the simple menu-based network.
candidates.where_now: SDF documents Gopher browsing from its shell, including its own Gopher root menu.
candidates.note: The operator documentation establishes continued client support and a documented SDF endpoint. Direct Gopher availability was not independently tested. No claims about server counts, audience growth or universal proxy availability are made.

rating.note: Editorial score; images and device review required before promotion.

candidates.name: SAN FRANCISCO TROLLEYBUSES
candidates.headline: The poles still trace the wires. The batteries now bridge the gaps.
candidates.why_survives: Electric trolleybuses suit frequent hilly routes and combine quiet operation with long vehicle life.
candidates.where_now: San Francisco Muni operates North America’s largest trolleybus fleet with New Flyer vehicles.
candidates.note: Verified 11 October 2026 against SFMTA’s current fleet page. The claim is continued operation in San Francisco, not that trolleybuses remain common everywhere; modern vehicles can travel short distances off-wire using batteries.

rating.note: Direct current-agency evidence and a highly legible visual; geographically specific rather than a universal survival claim.

candidates.name: RADIO STATION WWV
candidates.headline: The clock still speaks through static, one second at a time.
candidates.why_survives: Radio distributes standard time, frequencies and propagation information without requiring internet access.
candidates.where_now: NIST station WWV broadcasts continuously on multiple high-frequency channels from Colorado.
candidates.source_name: National Institute of Standards and Technology
candidates.note: Verified 12 October 2026 against NIST’s active station page and current broadcast specifications. The page states 24/7 service on five standard frequencies plus an experimental 25 MHz signal; reception varies by propagation.

rating.note: Direct operator evidence and a century-scale survival story; broad public recognition is the limiting score.

candidates.name: TYPEWRITERS
candidates.headline: The keys still strike paper without opening an app.
candidates.why_survives: Specialist offices, secure institutions, collectors and distraction-free writers sustain a small typewriter market.
candidates.where_now: Swintec currently lists manual and electronic typewriters, ribbons and service supplies.
candidates.note: Verified 14 October 2026 against current Swintec product listings showing manual and electronic typewriters with prices and availability. This supports a specialist continuing market, not mass-market popularity or continuous production of every listed model.

rating.note: Current specialist product listings and a universally recognisable silhouette make a strong exhibit; evidence supports availability rather than a broad manufacturing-volume claim.

candidates.name: USENET
candidates.headline: The pre-Web discussion network still has working servers.
candidates.why_survives: Independent providers maintain distributed newsgroup servers and access through dedicated newsreader software.
candidates.where_now: Eweka currently offers Usenet subscriptions, server settings and newsreader support for active and archived groups.
candidates.note: Checked 20 October 2026. Eweka publishes current subscription and server-configuration instructions for its Usenet backbone. This verifies a maintained access service, not that every listed group has active discussion, that historical content is complete, or that every original server survives. Active access and archived articles are distinguished. Provider marketing about speed, retention and group counts is not repeated as an independently verified fact.

sources.name: Eweka support — Start Accessing Usenet Newsgroups
sources.supports: Current account, server and newsreader setup support.

rating.note: Strong pre-Web survival story and current operator evidence. Abstract server/newsreader imagery is less immediately distinctive than physical machinery.

candidates.name: BRITISH SEMAPHORE SIGNALS
candidates.headline: Colour lights dominate. Mechanical arms still clear trains on parts of Britain’s railway.
candidates.why_survives: Working legacy installations remain within an operating network while signalling modernisation proceeds route by route.
candidates.where_now: Network Rail confirms that some traditional mechanical semaphore signals remain in use on its network.
candidates.note: Checked 25 October 2026. Network Rail’s current signalling explainer states that traditional mechanical semaphore signals still exist on the operational network and distinguishes them from modern colour-light and cab signalling. Its Safety Central glossary defines semaphore arms and their mechanical or electrical operation. This verifies continued use somewhere on Network Rail, not a complete inventory, uninterrupted nineteenth-century equipment at every site, or a claim that semaphore remains common. Preserved museum and heritage-railway signals are outside the candidate’s evidence scope.

sources.name: Network Rail Safety Central — Jargon Buster
sources.supports: Defines operational semaphore signals as fixed mechanical arms, usually worked by wire from a signal box lever frame.

rating.note: Highly legible railway silhouette and direct current-operator evidence; recognition is regionally uneven and the survival story is evolutionary rather than a dramatic revival.

candidates.name: RACING PIGEONS
candidates.headline: The message went digital. The pigeons still race home.
candidates.why_survives: Fanciers, clubs and organised competitions sustain breeding, training and timed homeward flights.
candidates.where_now: The RPRA publishes current UK race bookings and its 2026 national performance awards.
candidates.source_name: Royal Pigeon Racing Association — National Awards 2026

sources.name: RPRA — Race programmes
sources.supports: Current bookings include 31 October 2026; a booking is not proof that a future liberation has occurred.

candidates.note: Checked 27 October 2026. RPRA's 16 September 2026 awards call asks for performances in the current racing year, with entries due 6 November. The current programme also lists a future 31 October booking. Together these document an active organised sport, not merely museum birds; the scheduled race is not treated as completed. This is domestic homing-pigeon racing, not a claim that pigeons remain a normal communications network or that every event takes place.

rating.note: Recognisable animal and clear current association evidence; the collection fit is the surviving practice rather than an endangered species.

candidates.name: MECHANICAL METRONOMES
candidates.note: Checked 30 October 2026.  The manufacturer currently lists mechanical clockwork models requiring no batteries. This verifies current product availability as a category, not popularity or uninterrupted manufacture.
candidates.headline: Apps can keep the beat. A pendulum still does it without batteries.
candidates.why_survives: Mechanical clockwork offers an independent, visible pulse without a screen or battery.
candidates.where_now: Wittner lists mechanical System Maelzel metronomes in its current product range.

rating.note: Provisional editorial rating; original artwork and device review required before promotion.
